title: Cha Ca Hanoi
notes: This is a famous dish from a 100 year old restaurant in Hanoi, North Vietnam called Cha Ca La Vong. In fact, it is the only dish they serve. Other restaurants in the area try to tap into their success (and tourist line ups) by adding it to their menus.

ingredientSections.heading: Cha Ca Hanoi
items: 700g Oceanwise Pacific Cod, or other firm white fish
8 heads Baby Bok Choy, sliced lengthwise
1 Cup Fresh Dill, picked from stem
1 Cup Fresh Mint, picked from stem
½ Bunch Green Onions, thinly sliced

methodSections.heading: Cha Ca Paste
steps: Combine everything in a small food processor and blend until smooth.

methodSections.heading: Nuoc Cham
steps: Combine all ingredients making sure sugar is dissolved.

methodSections.heading: Cha Ca Hanoi
steps: Soak the vermicelli noodles in cold water for about an hour. Strain and set aside.
Heat a large wok or fry pan and add a good splash of oil. Add the cod pieces and sear for about 30 seconds.
Toss in the Cha Ca Paste and a couple of pinches of salt.
Add the coconut milk, two good pinches of the fresh dill, the chilli and sliced baby bok choy. Toss thoroughly and then add the strained vermicelli. Mix gently so as not to break up the cod pieces.
Finish with the lime juice and fish sauce, add more of each if you prefer a greater depth of flavour.

Using tongs, divide the mixture into four deep bowls. In the centre of each bowl, add a generous amount of the remaining dill, cilantro, mint and green onions. Serve with a small side dish of the Nuoc Cham.
